name: Sgt. Weaver
summary: "Sargent Weaver Ex-Marine," Larry wrote of the man in VN-0014, inside the radio van. On 2026-09-12: "Weaver was a cool guy and hung out with me a lot." Larry thinks the night-time picture of him in the van (VN-0015) was "taken at nighttime by Weaver or Chapman." On Larry's last day on the mountain, it was Weaver who took his place: "captain Geutler (his spelling) came and got me and dropped off Sgt Weaver, he was a E5 specialist. He was an ex marine." His son's account of the bathroom shooting has Weaver arriving while the gunman was aiming at Larry.
researchNotes: Larry named him from the photograph on 2026-08-15 (giscus-vn-0014-c18032226). The 2026-08-09 vision pass had read the VN-0014 name tape as beginning 'WE...'; that is machine output (rule 4) and is not corroboration of the name. Corrected 2026-09-14 after research/site-audit-2026-09-14.md, which found this record presenting it as testimony and photograph converging; the patch description that stood here was also removed (the interview guide asks Larry what Weaver's pocket patch said). The bathroom-shooting account is his son's paraphrase (giscus-stories-c18035411). If the court-martial record is found (ledger #11), Weaver should appear in it as a witness. 2026-09-12 (giscus-vn-0014-c18415711, -vn-0015-c18415735): Larry's van crewing, "Day shift was probably 4 guys and night shift there was 1 guy", makes the crew small enough that a morning report listing one man should list the others. 2026-09-03 (giscus-stories-c18259364): the drop-off on the mountain, now linked.
